problem_motivation.content: Currently developed ferritic superalloys exhibit low high-temperature strengths, limiting their usage.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, currently developed ferritic superalloys still exhibit low high-temperature strengths, which limits their usage.

problem_motivation.content: Existing precipitation-strengthened ferritic alloys suffer from low high-temperature strength and insufficient lightweight characteristics.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, these emerging precipitation-strengthened ferritic alloys still face some drawbacks, such as the low high-temperature strength and not lightweight, which limit their applications.

problem_motivation.content: Previous work on a specific HEA system was hindered by the formation of brittle intermetallic phases causing cracking.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Our previous work discovered potential L2 1 precipitation-strengthened lightweight HEAs (LWHEAs) in an Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti system, but the formation of the brittle C14 Laves phase deteriorates their properties because the dissimilarity of crystal structures and different thermal expansion coefficients between the C14 Laves and BCC-base phases increase the tendency to crack [18] .

problem_motivation.content: The vast compositional space makes efficient screening of suitable alloys a significant challenge.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, the vastness of the compositional space poses a huge challenge for efficiently screening out suitable compositions.

prior_approach.content: Prior work has involved efforts in designing advanced ferritic superalloys.
prior_approach.evidence_span: significantly increased the efforts in designing advanced ferritic superalloys

prior_approach.content: Existing advanced HEA-design strategies combine physicochemical criteria, CALPHAD, data mining, and multi-objective optimization.
prior_approach.evidence_span: At present, a few advanced HEA-design strategies were reported by combining the physicochemical criteria, CALPHAD, data mining, and multi-objective optimization algorithm [21] , [22] , [35] – [37]

prior_approach.content: The CALPHAD approach is identified as the current method capable of obtaining accurate multicomponent phase diagrams without heavy experimental work.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The CALPHAD approach [38] – [40] is currently the only method that can be used to obtain multicomponent phase diagrams with enough accuracy for practical applications without the need of the heavy experimental work [41] .

prior_approach.content: Lattice-gas models are cited as a prior approach successfully used to predict order-disorder phase transitions in conventional and high-entropy alloys, despite known restrictions.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Still, such models are found to successfully predict the order-disorder phase transitions in a number of conventional and high-entropy alloys (HEAs) [3] , [33] , [65] – [68] .

prior_limitation.content: Existing ferritic superalloys are limited by low high-temperature strengths.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: currently developed ferritic superalloys still exhibit low high-temperature strengths, which limits their usage

prior_limitation.content: Trial-and-error experimental methods are inefficient for screening vast composition spaces due to high cost and time requirements.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: The trial-and-error experimental method is obviously not suitable, since it is extremely costly and time-consuming to experimentally screen the proper alloys in the vast composition space.

prior_limitation.content: The specific molar fraction of the target L21 phase in Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti HEAs was previously unknown, necessitating an assumption for the high-throughput screening criteria.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: The optimal molar fraction of the L2 1 phase is not known. Hence, we set it to be 0.05–0.5 at the application temperatures as a reasonable approximation.

prior_limitation.content: The current thermodynamic database requires improvement regarding the stability of the L21 phase, as evidenced by discrepancies between predictions and experiments.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: The microstructure discrepancy between the thermodynamic prediction and experimental observation indicates that our current thermodynamic database needs further improvement on the stability of the L2 1 phase.

prior_limitation.content: The full potential of the CALPHAD approach is limited by the low efficiency of computational tools to explore the entire composition and temperature space.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: Although the CALPHAD approach has been well accepted in the design and development of advanced materials [21] , [47] – [51] , its full potential has not been fully released due to the low efficiency to explore the entire composition and temperature space of a multicomponent system.

causal_claim.content: The yield strengths of the designed alloys are attributed to precipitation strengthening and atomic-level complexity rather than intrinsic deformation behavior alone.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Therefore, the high yield strengths of Alloys 1 and 8 are attributed to the precipitation strengthening, besides the effect of atomic-level complexity in HEAs.

mechanism_principle.content: The formation of different L21 morphologies (nanoscale precipitates vs antiphase domains) is driven by how closely the alloy's chemical composition matches the perfect L21 stoichiometry.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: For G2 (Alloys 2–7), their chemical compositions can exactly match the perfect L2 1 stoichiometry, resulting in the formation of the single-phase L2 1 phase in the form of APD. In contrast, for G1 (Alloys 1 and 8), their chemical compositions deviate far away from the perfect L2 1 stoichiometry, leading to the formation of nanoscaled L2 1 precipitates within the BCC matrix.

mechanism_principle.content: The atomic occupancy of the multicomponent L21 structure and its related phase-evolution rule provide a basis for improving the efficiency of high-throughput calculations.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Especially, the HTC can become more efficient when it is coupled with the deciphered atomic occupancy of the multicomponent L2 1 structure and its related phase-evolution rule.

hypothesis_statement.content: The study proposes that integrating high-throughput screening, multiscale modeling, and experimental validation is an efficient method for discovering advanced materials.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: This study shows that integrating high-throughput screening, multiscale modeling, and experimental validation proves to be efficient and useful in accelerating the discovery of advanced precipitation-strengthened structural materials tuned by the high-entropy alloy concept.

hypothesis_statement.content: The pace of discovering High-Entropy Alloys (HEAs) can be accelerated through the development and application of efficient computational screening methods.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Fortunately, the pace of discovering promising HEAs can, in principle, be accelerated by the development of efficient computational screening methods and tools [19] , [20] .

hypothesis_statement.content: Coupling high-throughput design with fundamental understanding of LWHEAs will accelerate the discovery of promising HEAs.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Therefore, the high-throughput design and the fundamental understanding of the discovered LWHEAs will accelerate the pace of discovering promising HEAs, especially for multicomponent systems.

evidence_result.content: Synchrotron XRD and TEM analysis confirmed the as-cast alloys consist of L21 and BCC phases with equiaxed grains, validating the predicted phases.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The synchrotron x-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns (Fig. 2a ) demonstrate that all the eight alloys in the as-cast states are composed of L2 1 and possible BCC phases without other intermetallic phases. All the eight alloys have equiaxed grains (Fig. 2b, c and Supplementary Fig. 2 ), indicative of a single-phase structure.

evidence_result.content: Metropolis Monte Carlo calculations determined the ordering transition temperatures (Tc) to be 1607°C for Alloy 1 and 1997°C for Alloy 7, predicting that Alloy 7 retains order at higher temperatures.
evidence_result.evidence_span: As indicated by the red arrows, the ordering transition temperature, T c , of Alloy 1 [1607 °C (1880 K)] is much lower than that of Alloy 7 [1997 °C (2270 K), far beyond its melting temperature], suggesting that the ordered L2 1 phase is less easily retained in the solid state in Alloy 1 than in Alloy 7

constraint.content: The high-throughput predictions are valid only within a specific composition range (Al < 25 at.% and Mn > 15 at.%).
constraint.evidence_span: Especially, the HTC can become more efficient when it is coupled with the deciphered atomic occupancy of the multicomponent L2 1 structure and its related phase-evolution rule. Therefore, the high-throughput design and the fundamental understanding of the discovered LWHEAs will accelerate the pace of discovering promising HEAs, especially for multicomponent systems.

constraint.content: Compression tests are constrained to a specific strain rate of 2 × 10 −4 s −1.
constraint.evidence_span: Room and elevated-temperature compression tests of these eight alloys were carried out at the strain rate of 2 × 10 −4 s −1

constraint.content: The APT experiment is constrained to a specific laser pulse energy, pulse width, base temperature, and detection rate.
constraint.evidence_span: The APT experiment was run, employing a CAMECA LEAP 4000XHR in a laser mode with 60 pJ, 10-ps-laser pulsed, a 30K-base temperature, 0.5% detection rate
